problem: Hospital software was complicated and disconnected, so doctors and nurses spent more time clicking through prompts than caring for patients.
business_model: B2B SaaS cloud platform for hospitals (CareOS with CareHub, Mara, Insight and Backbone modules)

founders.name: Gautam Sivakumar
founders.background_notes: healthcarediscovery.ai says he grew up in Northern England, programmed as a teenager, practiced as a doctor, sold his flat and applied to YC. The YC page lists him as the only founder and gives no background.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company. PitchBook reportedly records out of business on 2021-04-14.

competitors.name: Medigram
competitors.what: Secure, legal alternative to texting among doctors in hospitals

technical_complexity.rationale: Clinical workflow software that must integrate with hospital systems and meet HIPAA hosting rules is standard enterprise engineering with compliance burden.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital deployments and integrations create switching costs, and HIPAA compliant hosting is a barrier, but electronic health record vendors control the data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Medisas. The company sold into hospitals through 2019 and is now listed out of business by databases.

market_need_then: The founder says he found hospital software unusable as a practicing doctor, and the company claimed care teams for half a million patients. No 2013 market data was found.

branding.domain_note: medisas.com is the company domain per YC page and was live in this fetch.

identity.visual_style: Product suite named CareOS, CareHub, Mara, Insight and Backbone
identity.voice_and_tone: Presents as the operating system for hospitals

brand_strength.rationale: Only trademark filings for MEDISAS in 2014 and directory pages were found, no press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Medisas raised about 10.6 million dollars in December 2016 and reportedly had about a million patients on its platform in 2019, then databases record it out of business in April 2021. The cause is not public: no post mortem was found, so failure factors stay empty, and sources disagree whether it closed since its own website still described its products.
notes: The Series A figure comes from a Form D (filed 2016-12-15, 10,589,641 dollars sold, 39 investors, SEC CIK 0001692364) as summarized by healthcarediscovery.ai, with CB Insights and Persana reporting a similar 10.6M Series A; I did not open EDGAR directly. Investor names come from an archived company site and a Rabois investment list as relayed by the same directory, and the Form D itself names no fund. The 2013 seed entry rests on CB Insights with no amount. Status conflicts: PitchBook, Tracxn and Seedtable say closed, CB Insights says alive, and medisas.com was live with placeholder text. The Medigram source is dated 2012-05, eight months before the batch.
